title: Remove tk tell, tk channel and the transport seam from ticks
description:
Make ticks factory-free. This is a removal, not a relocation into ticks — nothing here gets a ticks replacement.

GOES:
- cmd/tk/cmd/tell.go (317) and channel.go (634) with their tests. tell.go already exits 4 without a channel and its only channel is Telegram (channel.go:37: 'the only channel implemented today'), so both are entirely remote-notification features.
- internal/operator/telegram/** — 2,171 non-test lines across channel.go 756, client.go 848, factory.go 460, markdown.go 107, plus 1,852 test lines and the fakebot subpackage.
- The Channel interface and its capability interfaces (Adopter, ContextualChannel, FormattedSender, AttachmentSender) in internal/operator/channel.go, AND Consumer in engine.go. These are the IN-PROCESS transport extension point; the CLI replaces them. An interface with no implementation left in the tree is a stub, not a seam.
- cmd/tk/cmd/factory_operator.go, channel_context.go — check each; they exist to bridge the two.

STAYS, and getting this wrong breaks the product line: PendingStore, Pending, Question, mapping, locking, markdownlite.go (the store's formatting, used by the terminal path — telegram/markdown.go is Telegram-specific escaping and goes), the parking half of tk ask, and tk answer / approve / reject.

TWO THINGS TO RESOLVE RATHER THAN ASSUME:
- cmd/tk/cmd/ask.go imports operator.Channel. Work out which half of ask that is. Parking a question must survive; delivering it to a phone must not.
- .tick/operators.json maps operator identities and has readers beyond channel.go. Find them all before deleting anything. The mapping outliving the transport is likely correct — the factory will need it — but that is a finding to confirm, not a guess.

RUN TICK 1fd'S OFFLINE GUARD AFTER, and note that guard was written BEFORE this change precisely so it proves the removal did not take the terminal path with it.

WHAT IS DONE AND BUILDING at 80ea31b8: internal/operator/telegram/** deleted; Channel, Consumer, config.go, context.go, fake.go removed from internal/operator; cmd/tk/cmd/{tell,channel,channel_context,factory_operator}.go deleted; ask.go, answer.go, herd_wait.go and internal/herd/relay/relay.go repointed. The question store survives — engine.go, pending.go, mapping.go, question.go, markdownlite.go, the locks. 'go build ./...' passes and internal/operator, internal/herd/relay and cmd/tk all pass their tests.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is a refactor rather than the import fix it looks like: cmd/tk/cmd/answer_test.go still imports the deleted telegram and fakebot packages, so that one package fails to compile its tests. All TEN of its tests obtain their fixture through a bot-backed askTestEnv helper — so most of them are terminal-answer tests that merely happen to be built on transport scaffolding, and separating those from the genuinely transport-only ones (TestStalePressAfterAnswerIsAcknowledgedOnly builds an operator.Consumer over a telegram.Channel and asserts a stale Telegram button press) is judgement, not mechanics.

The offline guard from tick 1fd has not been run against this state yet, because the package it lives in does not compile.
acceptance_criteria: No Go code in ticks calls the Telegram Bot API and no bot token is read by tk. tk tell and tk channel are gone, with no stub or commented-out remnant. The question store, markdownlite and the terminal path remain; tick 1fd's offline guard passes after the removal. Every reader of .tick/operators.json is accounted for. go test ./... green.
